why_relevant: Monet+ (Switchio) is the single most competitively relevant CZ actor for a payments vendor: it runs ČSOB's central transaction/authorisation system for 60k+ POS terminals and ~2M transactions/day, plus transport ticketing (open-loop EMV in ~20 CZ cities) and private/fleet card schemes. Reference pages state incumbency, scale and scheme coverage.

source_name: Asseco Central Europe — Výroční zprávy (annual reports archive)
why_relevant: Bilingual CZ/EN annual reports with segment reporting; historically discloses banking-segment revenue and named financial-sector customers across CZ/SK/HU. The multi-year PDF archive supports revenue-concentration and win-timeline analysis that no marketing page provides.

Mid-size CZ integrator whose reference pages name banking-group subsidiaries (e.g. Identity Server for ČSOB Stavební spořitelna / ČMSS, multichannel infrastructure, SSO). Useful for mapping identity/authentication sub-vendors inside KBC-group entities in CZ.

Aricoma (KKCG) is the largest CZ IT group and consolidates AutoCont, Cleverlance, AEC, DataSpring etc. Its customers/references pages and press releases name banking clients (Komerční banka, Kooperativa) and ČSOB SAP S/4HANA work; the group structure page is itself a pointer to a dozen operating subsidiaries with their own bank references.

Global outsourcer with a large CZ delivery footprint; its newsroom announced the ČSOB business-process-transformation deal (Camunda BPM platform implementation, June 2026) — an example of the integrator disclosing a bank programme and its underlying product OEM that the bank did not announce.

Digital product studio delivering mobile banking for J&T Banka, with detail on security regime (OWASP MASVS testing, penetration tests). Shows which banks outsource mobile app builds to boutiques rather than to core integrators — a distinct procurement channel.

Unicorn (Vladimír Kovář group) sells banking software and large-scale integration in CZ/SK; its banking vertical page and reference/press sections indicate product lines and sector positioning, and its group includes Unicorn University and Unicorn Systems delivery arms.

Brno-based software house with a dedicated banking/fintech vertical page (AI-ready platforms, secure cloud for financial institutions) — a second-tier competitor not on the original actor list, surfaced by Czech-language search. Confirms the snowball value of local-language vertical landing pages.

Niche CZ supplier with an explicit banks-and-financial-institutions reference vertical; a new actor found only via local-language search. Useful for mapping the long tail of sub-vendors below the top-10 integrators.

CZ software house publishing a consolidated reference/case-study page; repeatedly surfaced across two independent Czech queries for bank case studies, suggesting financial-sector delivery content. Long-tail supplier mapping.

source_name: Veřejný rejstřík a Sbírka listin (or.justice.cz) — filed financial statements and annual reports
why_relevant: Statutory filing archive: every CZ integrator (Trask Solutions a.s., Adastra, Profinit, Monet+, Cleverlance Enterprise Solutions, Aricoma Systems, GEM System, Asseco CE a.s. IČO 27074358) must deposit účetní závěrka and výroční zpráva. Gives audited revenue, headcount, related-party structure and sometimes segment/customer-concentration notes — the only non-marketing evidence of how big the bank business really is.

source_name: CIOtrends / Computerworld CZ — TOP 100 ICT companies ranking and vendor coverage
why_relevant: Annual self-reported revenue ranking of CZ ICT companies plus per-vendor tag pages (e.g. /n/cleverlance/) and the yearly 'Případová studie' award writeups — an aggregator that both ranks the integrator field and points to individual bank project narratives.

source_name: Lupa.cz / CzechCrunch / Ekonom — CZ tech business press on integrator revenues and M&A
why_relevant: Czech business/tech press reports integrator revenues, group restructuring and acquisitions (Cleverlance ES passing CZK 1bn; Cleverlance acquiring AEC; Aricoma consolidation under KKCG) far earlier and more plainly than the filings. Bridges the gap between annual filings and vendor PR.

source_name: Czech job boards as integrator-project signal (Jobs.cz / Prace.cz / VímVíc / pracevtrasku.cz)
why_relevant: Job ads are the least-censored disclosure channel: they name the client sector, the core banking/card platform, and the technology being staffed, and headcount trajectory proxies each integrator's bank workload. Company profile pages also give a stable numeric company id usable as a join key across jobs.cz/prace.cz.

source_name: Finmag / Chytrý rejstřík — commercial mirrors of the CZ company register
why_relevant: Third-party mirrors of obchodní rejstřík and sbírka listin that are far easier to fetch than or.justice.cz (clean URLs by IČO, paginated document lists, occasional pre-extracted financials). Useful fallback when the official UI's session/captcha flow blocks automation.

State export-agency directory of Czech fintech and banking-technology vendors — a curated actor list produced by an organisation whose job is to enumerate exporters. Good for discovering payment/banking software houses missing from the seed actor map.

source_name: Comgate – nápověda / e-shop platformy a integrace
why_relevant: Comgate's own documentation enumerates every e-commerce platform, accounting package and POS system it integrates with (Shoptet, WooCommerce, PrestaShop, Magento, Shopify, Pohoda, Money S3, ABRA FlexiBee). This is a machine-enumerable partner/integration directory that reveals the whole CZ e-commerce vendor ecosystem around one of the largest domestic gateways.

Primary source for one of the leading Czech PSPs/gateways: pricing, payment methods, instalment partners (Cofidis, ESSOX, Home Credit), terminal offering (Nexgo hardware) and press/news. Direct evidence of product moves and partnership cadence.

GoPay is a major CZ/SK gateway; its blog publishes volume statistics (65m payments 2023, 90m 2024), new payment-method launches and partner integrations. Volumes and method launches are a proxy for competitive position.

source_name: GoPay help centre – integration docs, pricing and T&Cs
why_relevant: Publishes the current price list and gateway terms of use (e.g. conditions effective 1.4.2025) plus REST API v3 integration specs. Pricing/T&C documents are dated and versioned — an unusually hard signal for competitive pricing and scheme pass-through changes.

Directory of implementation partners and integration offers (e.g. PayU, Klarna gateway integrations). Reveals which gateways are being demanded/implemented and which agencies serve the acquiring ecosystem — a second-order partnership layer banking sources never show.

Largest CZ acquirer/terminal estate (took over Česká spořitelna's acquiring and card centre; JV since 2016). Site carries terminal pricing (from 0.65% per transaction), GP webpay online gateway, softPOS-style app-instead-of-terminal offer and switch-to-us campaigns aimed at competitors' merchants. Direct competitive intelligence on the CZ terminal estate.

Worldline runs a Czech entity and is a major processor/terminal supplier in CEE; the localized cs-cz site is the place where CZ-specific bank processing deals and product launches surface, in Czech, ahead of group-level English releases.

Dedicated merchant-acquiring site of ČSOB (KBC group): terminal portfolio, SoftPOS product, merchant manuals, and dated commercial terms PDFs for card acceptance. The PDFs give versioned, citable evidence of pricing/rule changes in CZ acquiring.

source_name: Komerční banka – KB SmartPay (merchant acquiring brand)
why_relevant: KB's merchant acquiring is marketed under the KB SmartPay brand (a Worldline/KB arrangement) and appears repeatedly in POS/ECR integration documentation as a distinct terminal estate. Needed to complete the acquirer map alongside Global Payments and ČSOB.

Scheme press releases in Czech announce bank partnerships, country leadership changes, programme launches (e.g. Strive Czechia, ~250k entrepreneurs) and portfolio wins/losses. Schemes BENEFIT from announcing integrations, so this is a high-yield partnership feed.

The second scheme leg of the CZ landscape; scheme-side confirmation of issuer portfolio moves (e.g. Česká spořitelna's reported migration from Mastercard to Visa) and merchant/fintech partnerships. Needed for balance against Mastercard's feed.

source_name: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) – statistics and quarterly press releases
why_relevant: The CZ card industry association publishes quarterly/annual market statistics (351k terminals in 2024 vs 323k in 2023; 319k contactless; 24.7k card-accepting e-shops) plus a members/observers list (18 members, 23 observers) that doubles as an actor map of issuers, acquirers and processors. Both a benchmark series and a POINTER to the member set.
